newsitem.title: NORWAY: Higher R&D costs hit Nera's 9-month result.
newsitem.headline: Higher R&D costs hit Nera's 9-month result.

text.p: Norwegian telecommunications group Nera ASA attributed higher research and development costs to a near five percent slip in operating profits in the first nine months 1996 compared with a year ago.
Nera posted an operating profit of 111.3 million crowns to September 30 against 116.8 million crowns in the corresponding 1995 period.
The company said orders received amounted to 2.13 billion crowns, a rise of about eigth percent from a year ago, but profits before tax dipped almost seven percent to 90.26 million crowns.
Nera said orders increased most in the area of transmission systems. Order backlog for the company totalled 1.5 billion crowns, of which 765 million will be invoiced during the fourth quarter.

"In spite of good orders and great activity in the market for transmission systems, we have not yet received as much income from our increased capacity in this field as we could have wished," said Nera President Asbjoern Birkeland in a statement.

"This is partly due to circumstances, but is also partly due to the fact that it takes time to realise earnings from newly-established offices and an increased number of sales representatives. From our eveluation of market prospects, conditions appear to be goodf for increased orders and operating revenues from this area."
Nera said group earnings were also weakened because a factory acquires in Great Britain had so far not met up to expectations.
"Much time and resources have been invested in increasing production volume," said Birkeland. He said he expected operation of the factory to show an improved performance during the fourth quarter.

The company's other core business, mobile satellite communications, maintained sales on about the same level as last year, but orders declined around 20 percent from the year-ago period due to postponed decisions regarding the building of land earth stations, Nera said.
"The delivery of land earth stations for Inmarsat's Mini-M service is on schedule and by the end of the year Nera will have delivered six land earth stations for this new service," Nera said.
The group said it had also received around 2,000 orders for its new lightweight satellite telephone, Nera WorldPhone.
